name: Nebius
founded: 2024 as Nebius (ex-Yandex N.V., est. 2000; Russia divestment completed July 2024, Nasdaq trading resumed October 2024)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Nebius is the fastest-compounding public neocloud and CoreWeave's most direct challenger — Q2 2026 revenue $582.3M (+454% YoY, beat), ARR $3.0B (+56% QoQ), AI-cloud adjusted-EBITDA margin ~50%, and >$40B of customer commitments anchored by Microsoft (up to ~$19.4B, served from Vineland, NJ) and Meta (up to ~$27B) — funded by a ~$20B, 20-month capital cascade that culminated in a $5.0B convertible priced August 19, 2026 and the company's first asset-backed debt ($775M at SOFR+250, July 2026). The stock rose 34% on the Q2 print. BACKGROUND: Amsterdam-headquartered remainder of Yandex N.V. after the July 2024 Russia divestment (~$5.2–5.4B, a Kremlin-required ~50% discount — the largest corporate exit from Russia since the invasion); founder Arkady Volozh returned as CEO after EU sanctions on him were lifted in March 2024. ~1,500 employees, mostly ex-Yandex engineers. SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX rates Nebius Gold — top of the tier, 'the most direct competitor to CoreWeave.' FY2026 guidance: revenue $3.0–3.4B, exit ARR $7–9B, ~40% EBITDA margin, capex $20–25B; contracted-power target raised to 5 GW by year-end 2026. Live risk: two stop-work orders at Vineland in August 2026 (unpermitted fuel-cell/LNG work) sit directly on the Microsoft contract's critical path.
ecosystemRole: We assess Nebius as the demand-side counterweight to CoreWeave in this ecosystem — the neocloud that validates hyperscaler-overflow economics (Microsoft, Meta) while running a genuinely full-stack software strategy (Token Factory inference, Tavily agentic search, in-house cloud software) rather than a pure landlord model. For power-chain vendors the read-through is direct and current: Nebius is building owned gigawatt-scale AI factories (Independence MO 1.2 GW, Pennsylvania up to 1.2 GW, Finland 310 MW), signed a $2.6B/10-year Bloom Energy master agreement for behind-the-meter solid-oxide fuel cells (first deployment 328 MW at Vineland — chosen partly because fuel cells avoid the Clean Air Act PSD review gas turbines trigger), and exports recovered heat at scale in Finland. Basis: company disclosures, CNBC/DCD coverage, and the ClusterMAX review; its 5 GW contracted-power target implies one of the largest open procurement books among neoclouds through 2027.

productsAndServices.name: Nebius AI Cloud ('Aether' platform)
productsAndServices.description: Full-stack AI-native cloud: non-virtualized GPU instances (GB300 NVL72, GB200 NVL72, HGX B300/B200/H200/H100, RTX PRO 6000) on non-blocking Quantum-2/X800 InfiniBand, with managed Kubernetes and Soperator (Slurm-on-K8s), AI storage (>500 GB/s shared filesystem), observability, and enterprise governance. Published on-demand pricing: HGX B300 $7.85/GPU-hr, B200 $7.15, H200 $4.50, H100 $3.85 (preemptible roughly half). Quarterly 'Aether' releases (3.0 → 3.6) added SOC 2/HIPAA/ISO compliance, Serverless AI, customer-managed keys, and the Nebius Echo natural-language infrastructure agent.
highlights: ClusterMAX Gold across 1.0/2.0/2.1 — top of tier with Oracle and Azure; praised for bare-metal-equivalent K8s VMs and 'realistic pricing right on the homepage'
NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud on H200 and GB300 NVL72; first in Europe to run HGX B300 in production
productsAndServices.positioning: SemiAnalysis: 'the most direct competitor to CoreWeave' — differentiated by Kubernetes-native flexibility vs CoreWeave's bare-metal long-reservation model; flagged weaknesses are colocation-deal sourcing, credit ratings, and lingering 'Russian roots' customer hesitancy.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Three deal types (company framing, 2026): short 3–6-month contracts at premium pricing ($40–50M/MW opportunity), core 1–3-year mid-term contracts, and long-term investment-grade contracts used to raise secured debt. Q2 2026 deals averaged >$20M revenue per MW, ~70% with prepayments covering 50–60% of capex.
targetSegments: AI-native startups (Cursor, Black Forest Labs, Recraft, Photoroom)
Four Q2 2026 deals >$1B TCV each: Reflection, Cohere, a US AI lab, a US quant firm
productsAndServices.roadmap: Vera Rubin NVL72 systems received and in validation (H2 2026); capacity auctions piloted; >1 GW/year deployment pace from 2027.

productsAndServices.name: Nebius Token Factory (inference platform) + AI software acquisitions
productsAndServices.description: Production inference platform (launched Nov 2025): 60+ open models behind an OpenAI-compatible API, sub-second dedicated endpoints, 99.9% SLA, autoscaling past 100M tokens/minute, zero-retention with EU/US residency, fine-tuning and distillation cutting cost up to 70%. Reinforced by acquisition: Tavily (agentic web search, $177.3M, 2.5M+ developers), Eigen AI (inference optimization, 'ranked #1 by NVIDIA at GTC 2026'), and Clarifai's core team + inference IP (founder Matthew Zeiler joined as SVP Research).
highlights: Inference workloads >3x QoQ in Q2 2026, increasingly agentic
Prosus runs up to 200B tokens/day at a 26x cost reduction vs proprietary models
productsAndServices.positioning: The software layer is the anti-commoditization play — margin and stickiness a pure GPU landlord lacks; day-one support for new open models (Kimi K3, GLM-5.2) with benchmark-verified accuracy parity.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Per-token pricing (shared and dedicated endpoints), self-serve and enterprise.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Frontier-AI research unit under Zeiler (agentic reasoning, world models, token efficiency, long-term memory).

productsAndServices.name: Committed-capacity contracts & data-center platform
productsAndServices.description: The contracted backbone: Microsoft (signed Sep 2025 — up to $17.4B through 2031, expandable to ~$19.4B, nine tranches of dedicated capacity at Vineland, NJ, all delivered on time to date) and Meta (agreement #1 ~$2.9B signed Nov 2025, fully in servicing; agreement #2 signed Mar 2026 — up to $27B: $12B dedicated clusters deploying H1 2027 plus up to $15B of unsold-capacity purchases). Footprint: 16+ locations — owned Finland (original + 310 MW second site), Independence MO (1.2 GW, groundbroken May 2026), Pennsylvania (up to 1.2 GW), Alabama, Minnesota, Oklahoma; colocation/built-to-suit in Kansas City, Vineland, Paris, Iceland, UK (£1.7B, four sites), Israel, Spain, Estonia.
highlights: Customer commitments >$40B; >$9B of prepayments expected in 2026
Contracted power: >2 GW (Feb 2026) → >3.5 GW (May) → 5 GW YE2026 target (Aug)
Active power ~170 MW at YE2025; connected-power target 800 MW–1 GW YE2026 — the gap between contracted and active is the buildout
productsAndServices.positioning: vs CoreWeave: roughly 1/4 the revenue and ~40% the backlog ($40B vs $104B), but EBITDA-positive earlier, net-cash longer, and rated one tier below on ClusterMAX; 24/7 Wall St casts Nebius as the 'more defensive profile' of the pair.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Take-or-pay committed contracts financing secured debt; asset-light partnership model (July 2026) adds partner-owned data centers running Nebius designs and software for revenue-share/licensing — growth without the capex.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Bloom Energy fuel cells (first 328 MW at Vineland); Vineland Phase 2 approved Aug 18, 2026 after stop-work orders; full Vineland operational capability now projected 2027.

productsAndServices.name: Group ventures & equity stakes
productsAndServices.description: Avride (consolidated): autonomous ride-hailing and delivery robots — commercial robotaxi on Uber in Dallas (Dec 2025), 200+ AV fleet, >60,000 Uber rides, 316,000+ US robot deliveries in 2025, backed by up to $375M from Uber and Nebius. TripleTen (consolidated): AI/tech reskilling bootcamps, FY2025 revenue $54.1M (+88%). Equity stakes: ClickHouse (~$15B Jan 2026 round — produced a $780.6M paper gain in Q1 2026) and Toloka (AI data; deconsolidated 2025 after a Bezos Expeditions-led round).
highlights: Avride FY2025 revenue just $1.3M — an option, not a business yet
The ClickHouse stake alone has generated >$1.3B of cumulative revaluation gains through the P&L
productsAndServices.positioning: Legacy-of-Yandex optionality; analysts value the stakes as a balance-sheet cushion rather than operations.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not applicable — consolidated ventures and minority stakes.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Avride pushing toward no-vehicle-operator robotaxi operations; potential monetization of stakes remains a funding lever.

recentDevelopments.headline: Microsoft agreement: ~$17.4B over five years (up to ~$19.4B), dedicated capacity from Vineland, NJ; stock +48% next day; $4.2B raised within the week ($3.16B converts + $1.15B equity)
recentDevelopments.read: The deal that created the investable Nebius — a hyperscaler validating a neocloud two tiers down the rating scale, and the template (contract → raise capital → build) every quarter since has followed.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Nebius has converted itself from spot GPU rental into a contracted compute utility, and that the >$40B backlog is the load-bearing asset. Basis: Microsoft (~$19.4B ceiling) and Meta (up to $27B) both structured take-or-pay with tranche deliveries all on time to date, >$9B of 2026 prepayments expected, and Q2 2026 deal economics ($20–25M ACV/MW, 70% prepaid, sub-2-year payback) that no on-demand business produces.

(High confidence) We assess the financing engine is inseparable from the operating model: ~$20B raised in ~20 months (three convert programs totaling ~$13.5B, $1.85B of strategic equity including NVIDIA's $2B warrant, ~$2.8B ATM, $775M secured debt) against FY2026 capex guidance of $20–25B on $3.0–3.4B of revenue. The July 2026 secured facility began the pivot from dilution to asset-backed debt — the same coupon-compression arc CoreWeave traveled — but the model stays capital-markets-dependent through at least 2027.

(High confidence) We assess customer concentration is the thesis-level risk, sharpened by Meta's reported 'Meta Compute' plans. Basis: 20-F discloses two customers at 25%/15% of 2025 revenue and one at 83% of credit exposure; three customers ≈59% of revenue by Q2 2026; the July 2026 reports that Meta may monetize its own excess GPUs turn the second anchor into a potential competitor — TipRanks calls any Microsoft/Meta renegotiation 'a thesis-breaking event.'

(Moderate confidence) We assess the full-stack software layer (Token Factory + Tavily + Eigen + Clarifai IP) is a genuine differentiator against landlord neoclouds, but not yet a proven P&L segment. Basis: inference workloads tripling QoQ, Prosus at 200B tokens/day, and ClusterMAX's praise for the software stack — against no disclosed standalone inference revenue. Collection gap: Nebius does not break out Token Factory economics.

(Moderate confidence) We assess execution risk has migrated from GPUs to permits and power. Basis: two Vineland stop-work orders in August 2026 (unpermitted fuel-cell/LNG work) with full capability slipping to 2027 on the Microsoft-dedicated site; the Bloom fuel-cell strategy is itself a permitting arbitrage; ICFR material weaknesses (fixed assets, TripleTen revenue) disclosed in the FY2025 20-F point to controls still catching up with 479% growth.
